newsitem.title: UK: Orange Order offer sympathy to Spain after murder.
newsitem.headline: Orange Order offer sympathy to Spain after murder.

text.p: The powerful Protestant Orange Order, scourge of banned IRA guerrillas in Northern Ireland, extended sympathy to Spain on Thursday after the murder of a young politician by ETA Basque separatists.

"We would not pretend to understand the politics of the Iberian peninsula and have no desire to interfere, but we recognise that murder is murder,'" the Protestant order's ruling body said in a statement.
The Order is a brotherhood whose 80,000 members in Britain's troubled Northern Ireland province hold controversial parades each summer celebrating Protestantism and supporting British rule.

The statement said the council, which is holding a meeting of some 100 representatives from countries that have Orange branches, had "offered its condolences to the family of the Conservative Councillor, Miguel Angel Blanco, murdered in Spain, and the Spanish people".
ETA separatists kidnapped Blanco last Thursday and executed him two days later.

"There are obvious similarities between the situation in Spain and that in Northern Ireland," said the Imperial Orange Council. "In each country there is a group prepared to use both the ballot box and the armalite (rifle) as their mood dictates."

The Irish Republican Army, one of western Europe's oldest and best equipped underground forces, is waging a 28-year war aimed at ending British sovereignty and uniting the province with neighbouring Catholic Ireland.
